'''Elliot Spiro Valenstein''' (December 9, 1923 – January 12, 2023) was an American psychologist who was [[professor]] of [[psychology]] and [[neuroscience]] at the [[University of Michigan]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Davidson|first=Keay|title=Author says medical fads could recur|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=N7krAAAAIBAJ&sjid=OvwFAAAAIBAJ&pg=5848,8356882&dq=elliot+valenstein&hl=en|accessdate=4 January 2011|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|date=25 February 1987}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last= Lewis, MD|first=Thomas H.|title=Blaming the Brain: The Real Truth About Drugs and Mental Health (review)|journal=[[Journal of the American Medical Association]]|year=1999|volume=281|issue=15|pages=1438–1439|doi=10.1001/jama.281.15.1438|url=http://jama.ama-assn.org/content/281/15/1438.extract|accessdate=4 January 2011|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He was an authority on [[Deep brain stimulation|brain stimulation]], [[psychosurgery]] and the history of psychiatry.

==Biography==
Valenstein was born in [[New York City]] on December 9, 1923, to Louis and Helen Valenstein (formally Spiro).{{citation needed|date=December 2020}} He fought in [[World War II]]. After returning from the war he attended [[City College of New York]] for his [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] and [[University of Kansas]] for his [[Master of Arts|M.A]] and [[PhD]].<ref>“Elliot Valenstein: U-M LSA Department of Psychology.” LSA, University of Michigan, lsa.umich.edu/psych/people/emeriti-faculty/esv.html.</ref>

Valenstein was the chief of the neuropsychology section at [[Walter Reed]] Institute Research from 1957 to 1961. He started teaching at [[University of Michigan]] in 1970.<ref>“Elliot Valenstein: U-M LSA Department of Psychology.” ''LSA'', University of Michigan, lsa.umich.edu/psych/people/emeriti-faculty/esv.html.</ref>

Valenstein was married to Thelma Lewis from 1947 until her death on December 13, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://obits.mlive.com/obituaries/annarbor/obituary.aspx?n=thelma-valenstein&pid=197307787|title = Thelma Valenstein Obituary (1926 - 2020) Ann Arbor News}}</ref> They have two children together; Paul and Carl. Valenstein died in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]], on January 12, 2023, at the age of 99.<ref>{{cite web |title=Elliot Valenstein obituary |url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/legacy/obituary.aspx?pid=203668280 |website=Legacy |access-date=16 January 2023 |date=16 January 2023}}</ref>

==Published books==
* ''Brain Control: A Critical Examination of Brain Stimulation and [[Psychosurgery]]'' (1973)
* ''Brain Stimulation and Motivation: Research and Commentary'' (Ed.) (1973)
* ''Great and Desperate Cures: The Rise and Decline of psychosurgery and other Radical Treatments for Mental Illness'' (1986), {{ISBN|0465027113}}
* ''Blaming the Brain: The Truth About Drugs and Mental Health'' (1998)
* ''The War of the Soups and the Sparks: The Discovery of Neurotransmitters and the Dispute over how Nerves Communicate'' (2005)
